Branch (a), which I expect: the 23 index rows are the only heading candidates in the document, they match the canonical titles well, so the pipeline resolves every item to a short index row at the very end of the file — the intc-2002 stub collapse of ADR-015 repeated exactly as that ADR predicted it would be, with each item scoring BASE_STRICT 0.95 because the heading text matched, and the total extracted length (the whole index is on the order of 2,000 chars) sitting above NO_EMPTY_SUCCESS_FLOOR = 1,000, so `no_empty_success` does NOT catch it and doc_status is likely `success_with_warning`. The min_chars floors are the checks that should go red. I expect branch (a) because the demo's own symptom, and interviewer 1's independent report (postmortem §8), was 'only short cross-reference/index fragments captured'. Branch (b): ADR-015's `_toc_runs` logic treats the trailing index as a table of contents and drops all 23 candidates, in which case every item comes back `missing` at 0.40 and the item_present checks go red instead. Either branch is a failure of this case and both are honest failure modes worth recording.
